newsitem.title: UK: Mark/Swiss tests new lows, other crosses steady.
newsitem.headline: Mark/Swiss tests new lows, other crosses steady.

text.p: The mark fell to a six-and-a-half month low against the Swiss franc in Europe as traders roiled by the dollar's slump against the yen fled to the traditional safe haven of Switzerland. The mark was little changed against most other European currencies in morning trade, despite gains it made against the dollar, amid lingering concern about Germany's fiscal outlook. "The moves in Europe are predominantly being driven by the dollar and the yen," said David Brickman, the European economist at Yamaichi International Europe. "The sharp move in dollar/yen has meant we have seen the normal safe haven flows" into the Swiss franc. Traders are looking to take their cue from the Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting later today. German April M3 data and the April Ifo survey this week and the first round of French parliamentary elections on Sunday are also expected to provide direction. The mark/Swiss franc rate fell earlier to 83.00 centimes, its weakest level since October 31. By 1034 GMT, it was trading at 83.05/07 from 83.60/65 Monday.

Expectations of a broad group of countries will launch European economic and monetary union on time continued keep a lid on mark gains. Concern that the mark will be subsumed into a single currency which is potentially weaker and less stable has held the mark back against other European currencies. "People have been concerned about Germany in terms of fiscal policy and this is giving rise to concern about the mark generally," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered. French President Jacques Chirac and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl are expected to reiterate their commitment to launching the single currency on schedule in 1999 when they meet in Paris later today. The mark has remained relatively stable against the French franc amid expectations the ruling centre-left coalition will win the parliamentary elections.
Mark/French franc stood at 3.3687/92 at 1000 GMT against 3.3690/93 late Monday.

"My concern is that the market is pricing in a centre-right win," said Brickman at Yamaichi. "The danger is that they have a very slim majority or that the National Front support the left in the second round because of their views on EMU, and this would be franc negative."
Mark/lira was off earlier lows but the Italian unit was still seen well-supported amid expectations of an Italian rate cut which some said could come as early as this week.
Italian cities preliminary May CPI data is due later today and Wednesday and analysts see May inflation falling to an annual rate of 1.5 percent from 1.7 percent in April.

Meantime, Italy's three-year programme of economic targets will be unveiled early next week and is expected to give new 1998 deficit forecasts and will be used as the basis for Italy's plans for first-wave EMU membership.
Against the lira, the mark stood at 983.75/90 from 980.50/1.00 Monday.
